newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to keep interest rates steady - Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Spain to keep interest rates steady - Reuter poll.

text.p: The Bank of Spain will keep its key money market interest rate unchanged at 7.25 percent at its regular repurchase tender on Tuesday, according to a Reuter poll.
Seven of eight economists and financial market dealers surveyed by Reuters on Monday said they expected the Bank of Spain to hold off on its sixth interest rate cut this year.
The other expert said there was a 50-50 chance the central bank would lower the rate by 25 basis points.

But the vast majority said the Bank of Spain would likely keep rates steady until it had more details on the 1997 budget, which the government will formally present by the end of September, and on August inflation data.
Uncertainty over the price data, due September 13, could also persuade the Bank of Spain to wait. A tobacco and alcohol tax rise is expected to push CPI up from July's 3.7 percent.
The Bank of Spain last lowered its key rate on June 4, bringing it down to 7.25 percent from nine percent at the beginning of the year.
